thread:
lia: dropped an nsys snapshot from the matmul perf run — weird algo flip under modest concurrency (3-4 inflight). link: gs://redwood-traces/nsys/1905002468
omar: looking now. initial skim shows repeated cudaMalloc/CUDA_FREE churn around the matmul windows, looks like workspace fragmentation
lia: exact. timeline shows cublasLt choosing a no-ws algo repeatedly after the 3rd concurrent request even though a ws-friendly algo exists earlier in the trace
tess: is this the run with kvcache warmup turned on? that can change memory layout across requests
lia: yes, kvcache enabled with prefix caching; KV cache warmups cause transient larger allocs -> slab rounding pushes matmul ws allocs into separate buffers
omar: guessed that. cuBLASLt heuristics can prefer an algorithm with smaller workspace when it sees tight available memory even if it's slower overall
ryan: can you paste the nsys cmd you ran? also any env vars (CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_POLICY etc)?
lia: command:
```
nsys profile -o /tmp/matmul_sweep -t cuda,nvtx,cudaProfilerApi --trace=nvtx,cuda --sample=none ./perf_runner --concurrency 4 --batch-sz 8
```
env: CUBLASLT_ALGO_CONFIG=auto, REDWOOD_KVCACHE=1, REDWOOD_WS_LIMIT=auto
lia: short perf excerpt from the timeline (kernel names trimmed):
```
T=0.12s cublasLtAlgo_12 ws=8192 time=0.9ms
T=0.17s cublasLtAlgo_7  ws=0    time=1.6ms
T=0.21s cublasLtAlgo_12 ws=8192 time=0.95ms
T=0.26s cublasLtAlgo_7  ws=0    time=1.65ms
```
omar: that alternating pattern screams workspace allocation contention. If the allocator rounds to different slab sizes when kvcache hits, the available contiguous block for the 8KB ws might disappear intermittently
tess: quick experiment: try forcing REDWOOD_WS_LIMIT=16MB or set CUBLASLT_ALGO_CONFIG to prefer algos 12/13
lia: did that in a quick run — p99 latency dropped ~18% and algo stabilized to 12 across the trace
perf-bot: perf-regression-checker detected a regression baseline=1899870001 current=1905002468 metric=p99 +12% -> filing perf-alert #PRF-3421
ryan: can we reproduce deterministically with kernel-replay? I want a kernel-level replay to test allocator patch without full infra
omar: I ran a kernel-replay build earlier; replaying the exact sequence (including KV cache allocs) reproduces the flip. patching allocator rounding to 64KB alignment stabilized behavior
lia: good signal. patch looks small but we should be careful about overall fragmentation tradeoffs
tess: also consider batching heuristic: the scheduler bumped batch to 8 which increases ws pressure — maybe cap batch growth when kvcache warms concurrently
lia: note for the perf PR: include nsys heatmap, kernel timeline snippet, and the small allocator diff + microbench for fragmentation
ryan: I'll add a deterministic repro harness using kernel-replay and upload an nvtx-annotated replay so we can run on CI
lia: thanks — I'll open the allocator PR and attach the nsys tarball. next steps: (1) run replay CI with allocator patch, (2) add an e2e that toggles kvcache warmup to catch future regressions, (3) tweak batching heuristic to respect transient ws pressure
tess: :thumbsup:
perf-bot: created issue: https://issues.redwood.ai/PRF-3421 (assign: lia, review: ryan, priority: high)
